title: Machine learning identifies predicted zero- and extreme-thermal-expansion monolayers
summary: High-throughput calculations and symbolic regression identified mechanical descriptors that classify positive- versus negative-thermal-expansion 2D crystals, then used those descriptors to predict monolayers with near-zero thermal expansion (2D Invar) and unusually large positive or negative expansion (anti-Invar). The paper reports multiple specific predicted crystals and explains the phonon/deformation-mode basis. The materials are computational predictions rather than experimentally synthesized monolayers.
ai_technology: High-throughput calculations combined with symbolic regression machine learning

evidence.tested: High-throughput calculations and symbolic regression identified mechanical descriptors that classify positive- versus negative-thermal-expansion 2D crystals, then used those descriptors to predict monolayers with near-zero thermal expansion (2D Invar) and unusually large positive or negative expansion (anti-Invar).
evidence.unknown: The identified materials and thermal-expansion properties are from computational/high-throughput predictions and were not experimentally validated in this paper. This is a new 2D monolayer property result, distinct from previously cataloged bulk high-entropy Invar alloys.
evidence.ai_role: Learned interpretable relationships between in-plane tensile stiffness, out-of-plane bending stiffness and thermal-expansion class, then used them to screen 2D-crystal databases for predicted Invar and anti-Invar materials.
